It is Makkan according to the majority.

Qatada said: It is Madinan.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Surat al-'Asr was revealed in Makkah.

al-Tabarani, in al-Awsat, and al-Bayhaqi, in al-Shu'ab, narrated from Abu Muzaynah al-Darimi, who was a Companion: "When two men among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) met, they would not part until one of them had recited Surat al-'Asr to the other, and then one of them had greeted the other with salam."

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

He, Glorified is He, swears by al-'asr, which is time (al-dahr), because of the lessons it contains: the passing of night and day according to a set measure of cycles, and the succession of darkness and light. In that is clear evidence of the Maker, Mighty and Majestic is He, and of His oneness. The night is called 'asr and the day is called 'asr. From this is the saying of Humayd ibn Thawr:

"The two 'asrs, a day and a night, never cease, when the two seek to attain what they have wished for."

The morning and the evening are also called the two 'asrs. From this is the saying of the poet:

"I put him off through the two 'asrs until he tires of me, and he accepts half the debt, his nose rubbed in the dust."

Qatada and al-Hasan said: What is meant by it in the verse is the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy), which is the time between the sun's passing the zenith and its setting. From this is the saying of the poet:

"'Amr sets out in the evening with us, and the 'asr has grown short; in the first evening journey lie gain and reward."

It is also narrated from Qatada that it is the last hour of the hours of the day. Muqatil said: What is meant is the 'Asr prayer, which is the middle prayer (al-salat al-wusta) that God, Glorified is He, commanded to be guarded. It is also said that it is an oath by the era of the Prophet (ﷺ).

al-Zajjaj said: Some said its meaning is "by the Lord of al-'asr," but the first view is preferable.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. This is the answer to the oath.

Khusr and khusran mean diminution and the loss of capital. The meaning is that every human being, in trades, endeavors, and spending lifetimes on the works of this world, is in deficiency and in straying from the truth until he dies.

It is also said that what is meant by "mankind" is the disbeliever. It is also said that it is a group of the disbelievers: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, and al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Asad. The first view is preferable because of the generality in the word "mankind" and because the exception points to it.

al-Akhfash said: "in khusr" means in destruction.

al-Farra' said: in punishment.

Ibn Zayd said: in evil.

The majority recited "wal-'asr" with sukun on the sad. They also recited "khusr" with damma on the kha' and sukun on the sin.

Yahya ibn Sallam recited "wal-'asir" with kasra on the sad.

al-A'raj, Talhah, and 'Isa recited "khusur" with damma on both the kha' and the sin, and this reading is also narrated from 'Asim.

They are in profit, not in loss, because they worked for the Hereafter and the works of this world did not distract them from it. The exception is a connected one (istithna' muttasil). According to the one who said that what is meant by "mankind" is only the disbeliever, it would be a disconnected one (munqati'). Under this exception falls every believing man and woman. There is no ground for the claim that what is meant is the Companions or some of them, for the wording is general, and no one who is characterized by belief and righteous action falls outside it. ﴿and advise one another to the truth﴾, that is, they enjoin one another to the truth that must be upheld, which is belief in God, tawhid (the oneness of God), observing what God has legislated, and avoiding what He has forbidden.

Qatada said: "to the truth" means to the Qur'an. It is also said: to tawhid. Taking it in the general sense is preferable. ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾, that is, patience in refraining from disobedience to God, Glorified is He, and patience in performing His obligations.

Making mutual counsel to patience a companion of mutual counsel to the truth is evidence of its great worth, its lofty honor, and the abundant reward of those who are patient in what patience is due. ﴿Indeed, God is with the patient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 153]. Moreover, counsel to patience falls under counsel to the truth, so singling it out by mention and specifying it by explicit text is among the greatest proofs of its eminence over the other qualities of the truth, its greater honor over them, and its higher rank above them.
